# BAD-067 — functions.test.mjs: the reviewer OTP test fails on the sixth local run in an hour

## Brief
`itest('/otp short-circuits the reviewer address without erroring')` in `test/server/functions.test.mjs` asserts 200. It fails with 429 on a long-lived local stack once the suite has run six times in an hour.

Why: `server/supabase/functions/otp/index.ts:49` limits `otp:${email}` to 5 per 3600s, and `REVIEWER_EMAIL` defaults to the constant `reviewer@badtakes.io` (`functions.test.mjs:62`). Every other address the suite uses is randomized per run (`buyer+ord_<ts>@example.com`, `stranger+u_<ts>@example.com`), and the IP buckets are too (`otp:ip:test-run-<id>`), so those reset each time and this one does not. Observed on the BAD-047 worktree stack: `private.rate_limits` held `otp:reviewer@badtakes.io` at count 7 in a window opened at 00:17, while every per-run bucket sat at 1 or 3.

Not a CI problem: a runner builds a fresh stack per run, so the counter starts at zero and one run charges it once. It is purely a local re-run papercut — but an expensive one, because the failure reads as a broken test in whatever branch happens to be the sixth run, and it cost two spudagents on BAD-047 an explanation apiece.

The obvious fix is to give the reviewer address the same per-run suffix as the others. Before doing that, check whether the *constant* is load-bearing: the reviewer short-circuit exists so App Review's fixed address gets a code without a purchase, and a test that randomizes the address may stop proving the thing it is named for. If it is, the alternative is clearing that one bucket in the suite's setup, the way a test that owns its fixture would.

Found by Spud while verifying BAD-047's PR 1, not by a spudagent; no proposal exists for it.

## Size, persona and model decision
One scout or engineer on sonnet; the fix is a per-run address, the judgement is whether the fixed one is load-bearing for what the test claims to prove.
